title: Pizza Quattro Stagioni
author: Marco Bellini
desc: 'Four Seasons' pizza divides its toppings into four quarters — mushrooms, artichokes, ham, and olives — each representing a season, all on the same slow-fermented Neapolitan base.
longDesc: Rather than mixing toppings together, quattro stagioni keeps each ingredient to its own quarter of the pizza, letting diners taste each season's character distinctly before they inevitably blend at the center.
ingredients: 500 g (4 cups) 00 flour or bread flour
300 g (10.5 oz) canned San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
150 g (5.3 oz) mushrooms, sliced and sautéed
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the water, then gradually mix in the flour and salt to form a shaggy dough.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth, place in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise at room temperature for 2 hours.
Divide into 4 balls, shape into tight rounds, and refrigerate covered for at least 8 hours, ideally 24.
Bring the dough to room temperature 1–2 hours before baking, and preheat the oven with a stone or steel to its highest setting for a full hour.
Sauté the mushrooms separately in a little olive oil until golden, and set aside with the other toppings prepared.
Stretch a dough ball by hand into a round and spread with a thin layer of crushed tomatoes.
Dot with mozzarella across the whole pizza, then arrange the mushrooms, artichokes, ham, and olives each in their own quarter.
Slide onto the hot stone and bake for 8–12 minutes until the crust is puffed and charred in spots.
Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and serve immediately.
chefTips: Pre-cook the mushrooms separately so they don't release excess water onto the pizza during baking.
Keep each topping distinctly within its own quarter rather than letting them mix, which is the whole point of this style.
A long, cold fermentation for the dough gives far more flavor than a same-day dough.
commonMistakes: Using raw, unsautéed mushrooms, which release water and make that quarter of the pizza soggy.
Mixing the toppings together rather than keeping them separated by quarter.
Overloading each quarter, preventing that section from cooking through properly.
storage: Best eaten fresh; leftover pizza keeps refrigerated for up to 2 days.
reheating: Reheat in a hot skillet or oven to re-crisp; avoid the microwave.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein and calcium, with vegetables contributing fiber and vitamins.
culturalNote: Quattro stagioni is a beloved variation across Italian pizzerias, its four distinct quarters a playful way to enjoy several classic toppings without any one overwhelming the others.
